description.value: The goal of the current study was to examine the neural correlates of emotional reactivity and cognitive reappraisal as a technique to achieve emotional regulation in GAD.

spans.text: The goal of the current study was to examine the neural correlates of emotional reactivity and cognitive reappraisal as a technique to achieve emotional regulation in GAD.

value: we hypothesized exaggerated amygdala reactivity in GAD, relative to HCs, when viewing negative images.
During reappraisal, we hypothesized that individuals with GAD, compared to HCs, would exhibit less engagement in cortical regions implicated in emotion regulation (e.g., IFG, DLPFC, DMPFC).

Behaviorally, we expected the GAD group to report feeling more negative than HCs in both the emotional reactivity and reappraisal conditions, reflecting greater subjective reactivity to negative stimuli and deficiency in dampening emotional response to negative stimuli.

spans.text: Based on existing literature and theory, we hypothesized exaggerated amygdala reactivity in GAD, relative to HCs, when viewing negative images. model_settings.value: A 2 (Group: HC, GAD) × 2 (Condition: emotional reactivity, emotion regulation) mixed-measures ANOVA was used, with condition as a repeated measure. Condition-specific contrasts were modeled relative to Look-Neutral. Significant clusters were required to meet whole-brain multiple-comparison correction using 3dClustSim with 10,000 iterations, voxel threshold p<0.001, cluster-level alpha<0.05, and a minimum cluster size of 60 voxels.
